title: Record parse errors name neither the file nor the record
body:
`Records::parse` (nail/src/io/records.rs) runs `Sequence::from_fasta` or `Profile::from_p7hmm` on one record. Their errors say what is wrong but not where. `read_queries` adds only `failed to parse query hmm` or `failed to build profiles`, and the target path adds `failed to write mmseqs target DB`. In a file of thousands of records the user cannot find the bad one.

Messages the input survey on nail-d551f7 saw from the release binary:

- `byte: "49" is not in the compressed amino acid alphabet`, for a `1` in a sequence; the residue prints as a decimal byte
- `no newline in FASTA record`, for a last record with no final newline
- `record 0 has no name`, for a p7hmm model with no `NAME` line
- `invalid utf-8 sequence of 1 bytes from index 1`, for a non-UTF-8 record name
- `failed to parse HMM float: "xyz"`, `expected 20 floats, got fewer`, `missing: match emissions 1`

## Proposal

`Records::parse` and `Records::name` wrap each error with the file path and the record's position, and its name when nail could read one. `Sequence::from_fasta` prints a bad residue as a character.

## Open

- whether a last FASTA record with no final newline should be an error at all; nobody has checked what HMMER does
close_reason: Records keeps its path and wraps parse and name errors with record position, name and file, in nail/src/io/records.rs. Sequence::from_fasta prints the residue as a char. The no-newline rows were stale, see note. Committed on dev.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/69ba1bc3
notes.text: Two rows of the table no longer hold on `dev`. A last record with no final newline, and a header-only last record, both run clean at `170dc79`, and `hmmsearch` reads each as two targets. `dev` moved to `libsail` 0.4.2 after the survey, and the `no newline in FASTA record` bail in `Sequence::from_fasta` is now unreachable from a file as far as I can tell. That answers the open question: HMMER accepts both.
